job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today in Geography class, we learned about the fascinating drainage systems of India. I was surprised to learn that Himalayan rivers like the Ganga and Indus are perennial not just because of rain, but because they are fed by melting snow from the glaciers throughout the year. We also discussed how India’s rivers do not all flow in one direction; while many flow east towards the Bay of Bengal, rivers like the Narmada and Tapi flow west into the Arabian Sea. Our teacher explained that a drainage basin is much more than just a river channel; it is the entire area of land that collects water and drains it into a single river system. Finally, we talked about the sad state of our rivers. Pollution is not just about industrial waste; it is also caused by untreated sewage from cities and agricultural runoff from farms. It is clear that protecting our water sources requires a much deeper understanding than I previously thought. I hope we can all contribute to keeping our rivers clean and healthy for the future.
response.summary: This diary entry explores the nature of Himalayan rivers, the diverse flow directions of Indian rivers, the definition of a drainage basin, and the multiple causes of river pollution. It emphasizes the importance of understanding these geographical concepts for environmental conservation.
